drafts.author: @shephyken
drafts.post_excerpt: Customer service is a philosophy, not a department. Customer service is everyone's job. Manage every customer touchpoint.
drafts.draft:
The 'manage every touchpoint' one is the hardest. Most companies manage the touchpoints they designed. The ones they didn't — a call that rings out, a hold that goes 7 minutes, a callback that never comes — those are also touchpoints. Invisible until a customer leaves.

Voice AI doesn't fix the philosophy problem. But it makes every invisible touchpoint visible. When every call is answered, logged, and resolved, 'manage every touchpoint' stops being aspirational. It becomes infrastructure.

drafts.author: @shephyken
drafts.post_excerpt: Consistency creates confidence. Customers like knowing what to expect. When experiences are predictable in a positive way, customers become comfortable doing business with you.
drafts.draft:
Consistency is the cheapest retention tool nobody builds for. Most contact center consistency problems aren't a culture problem — they're a staffing problem. Tuesday at 9am hits differently than Friday at 5pm. The new hire hits differently than the 10-year veteran.

The companies using voice AI aren't replacing humans. They're using AI to create a consistent floor — same speed, same tone, same resolution rate every time — so the human handles the edge cases that need actual judgment. Consistency stops being a training goal. It becomes infrastructure.

drafts.author: @shephyken
drafts.post_excerpt: Customers are willing to buy from you. The question is: are you making it harder than it needs to be?
drafts.draft:
The friction question usually gets answered wrong. Companies audit checkout flows but not hold times. They A/B test onboarding but not what happens when something goes wrong post-purchase.

The highest-friction moment for most customers isn't buying. It's the call they have to make six weeks later. Le Marquier moved 94% of those calls to full resolution without a human. Not because AI is cheaper — because the friction went to zero and the customer didn't have to fight for their outcome.

drafts.author: @jaybaer
drafts.post_excerpt: Who says you need a dev team to build an AI workforce? Custom AI agents were 'enterprise-only' toys. Now voice-first AI agents resolve requests end-to-end during the conversation.
drafts.draft:
The 'zero code' pitch misses the harder question: what does the agent actually resolve?

Most 'voice AI' systems are sophisticated IVRs. They answer, they qualify, then they transfer. The metric is still deflection — not resolution.

The bar that matters: does the customer hang up with the problem solved, or do they hang up to call someone else? Le Marquier runs 2,500 calls a month — 94% resolve without a human. Not because the tech is smarter, but because the workflow was designed around resolution, not deflection.

drafts.author: @shephyken
drafts.post_excerpt: What if gamifying customer service wasn't about competition, but about personal performance? Compete against yourself, not others.
drafts.draft:
The personal performance frame is where this gets interesting. The problem isn't that agents don't want to improve — it's that most contact centers give them lag indicators. You get your CSAT score three days after the call.

Voice AI changes what data is available in real time. Every call is scored, every resolution tracked, every pattern visible — not for surveillance, but for coaching. Gamification stops being a program and starts being built into the operating rhythm. The agent competing against themselves now has the data to actually do it.
